elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 4(a): "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — an unconditional Customer election, and the element is satisfied by the Agreement-level right (no Order Form structure exists here).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted Customer right requires "ninety (90) days written notice", three times the preferred 30-day maximum. To reach preferred the drafter would have to render the Customer notice period as thirty (30) days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language appears anywhere in the rendered paragraph; the only money sentence runs the other way ("Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period"). A pro-rata refund of prepaid fees obligation would have to be added.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained "Kubient may not terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit", plus the new limitation that Kubient's no-cause right is "effective only at the end of the then-current Term" — so no Kubient convenience termination takes effect during any committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band, and the timing bar was removed for Customer by limiting the Initial Term lock-in to Kubient, so the right is unconditional as to timing.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not bite: the retained sentence ("Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period") entitles Kubient only to revenue actually generated through the 90-day notice window, not a penalty payable on early exit; read even at its widest it cannot exceed roughly three months of fees. No separate early-termination fee, formula or instalment survives.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days written notice to Customer, effective only at the end of the then-current Term" — the effective date is expressly anchored to term end, satisfying the term-end-only requirement rather than a bare auto-renewal notice right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Kubient's no-cause right requires "ninety (90) days written notice to Customer".

reasons: Fallback level is complete on the face of the operative text: Customer gets an unconditional 90-day convenience exit, Kubient's no-cause right is expressly effective only at the end of the then-current Term on 90 days' notice, and no early-termination penalty survives beyond fees actually generated during the notice window.

Preferred fails on two elements only — the Customer notice period is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund — which is consistent with the drafter's stated decision to land at the fallback in a revenue-share deal with no prepaid fees.

'deviation' is the correct finding status: the original clause locked Customer in for the Initial Term and gave Kubient a no-cause right "following the Initial Term" untethered to term end, so it failed the fallback on a material term.

Minimality holds. The two edits (confining the Initial Term bar to Kubient, and splitting the mutual sentence into a Customer convenience right and a term-end-anchored Kubient right) are each required by a selected fallback element. Favourable retained language survives untouched — the breach cure right, the insolvency right, the fee-entitlement sentence and the auto-renewal mechanic — and no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra remedy was added.

Removal of the Customer half of the mutual Initial Term lock-in is inside the checklist, not an out-of-scope deletion: element 1 requires an unconditional Customer convenience right on 60–90 days' notice, which the retained "Neither Party may terminate ... during the Initial Term" would have blocked.

Intent is preserved: the Term/renewal structure, paragraph 4(b) cross-reference, Exhibit carve-out and fee allocation all survive without contradiction, and the edit creates no dangling reference or undefined new term (the pre-existing and unaltered phrase "the termination period" is inherited, not introduced).

If the client wants the preferred position, the two repairs are: change the Customer notice period to thirty (30) days, and add an express obligation that Kubient refund prepaid fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.
